A crystal radio made mostly from scrap around the house. A crystal radio is powered only by radio waves themselves.

I remember as a kid my Dad had a Moterola radio in his P.U. You had to buy a crystal per town. He bought 3 nearby towns + our hometown. Now I wonder how could he be charged for a radio wave? Please explainittomelikeimfive, thanks.

not an expert here, but as I understand it, this is how it works:

Radio waves are used to transmit sound. Your radio needs to transform these waves into audible sound, and for that, it needs a 'semiconductor'. Nowadays, a wide variety of electric semiconductors are available, but in the olden days, you had to use crystals. Thing is, every crystal can only convert one frequency of airwaves into sound. Therefore, you needed a crystal for every single frequency you wanted to listen to. These crystals needed to be manufactured and distributed, which made them a commercial product you need to pay for.
